column4: Visit note | 2025-10-18 11:00 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Salma Bepari, 75, female. Mrs. Bepari attends this follow-up review reporting a persistent fluttering sensation in her chest accompanied by occasional dizzy spells. She mentions that these symptoms first started while she was resting after a family lunch in Bashundhara. She is a homemaker and lives with her extended family in a busy neighborhood. She reports no prior history of major cardiac illness and denies chest pain or shortness of breath at rest. On examination today, her pulse 134 bpm and irregular, BP 126/77 mmHg, and weight 90 kg. Heart sounds are irregularly irregular with a fast ventricular rate, and her chest remains clear to auscultation bilaterally. Assessment: Atrial fibrillation. Plan: a prescription was issued for rate control and anticoagulation therapy. She was advised to limit tea and coffee consumption, avoid alcohol completely, and report any fainting episodes to the clinic at once. Follow-up is scheduled in 2 weeks with an ECG and kidney function tests.

Visit note | 2025-10-19 03:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Mahiya Mahmud, 44, female. Mrs. Mahmud returns for a review of her ongoing mental health concerns, reporting continued poor sleep and low energy levels that affect her daily activities. She works as a bus driver and explains that her low mood began after moving away from her family to Khilgaon. She notes that her sleep disturbances have persisted despite trying relaxation techniques at night. She denies any neurological deficits or chronic medical illnesses. On examination, her PHQ-9 score 15, BP 134/73 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, and weight 85 kg. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued for adjustment of her therapeutic regimen. She was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-10-19 03:30 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Arif Pramanik, 36, male. Mr. Pramanik presents for his first visit complaining of getting breathless on the stairs, looking pale, and experiencing constant tiredness throughout the day. He works as a fisherman and states that his fatigue started after a severe stomach illness during a stay in Sylhet. He has a known history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus managed with oral agents. He denies any chest pain, chronic cough, or bleeding manifestations. On examination, his haemoglobin 10.0 g/dL, BP 128/85 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, and weight 59 kg. Conjunctivae are pale, and systemic examination is otherwise unremarkable. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for iron supplementation. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin test.

Visit note | 2025-10-19 03:30 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Shapla Alam, 58, female. Mrs. Alam attends this follow-up visit for ongoing wheezing, coughing at night, and a tight chest whenever she is exposed to dust or cold air. She works as a nurse and notes that her respiratory symptoms flared during the recent winter smog in Bashundhara. She reports adherence to her current inhaler therapy but struggles with technique during acute flare-ups. She denies fever, weight loss, or smoking history. On examination, her SpO2 92% on room air, BP 134/82 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, and weight 70 kg. Auscultation reveals bilateral expiratory wheezes with prolonged expiration. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued for controller and reliever medications. She was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep her bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique from the nurse. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.
